decisions.statement: The whole answer is one JSON object carrying `types`, `properties` and `propertyTypes`.
A row is an `at` and a `values`.
A page type is answered with the properties that page type declares.
A property page is answered under the kind of property that page is.
A property carrying properties of its own is answered with those properties too.
Every row is read from the index rather than from a page body.
The three groups are handed back and the caller assembles the tree.
A property is named bare where that is unambiguous and `kind/slug` where the bare name is not.
A page type has `many` and `maxCount` and `required`.
The property page has the rest.
A declaration naming no property page refuses the whole answer.
A row names the checkout that row was read from ahead of the path inside that checkout.
The code answers as a file run on its own as well as through the index.
No group of domain rows is answered.
A run writes nothing.
The answer is drawn from the repository root or from a reading of the index.
Which page types are kinds of property is answered by the graph's `extended` closure.
A type above is reached by its path rather than by its slug.
The relation above is read as the index resolves it rather than as the body spells it.
A type naming the type above it by id is reached as readily as one naming it by slug.

definition: the command answering the page type and property rows a page tree is assembled from
